entry_state: The bank path separates deposits, settlement cash, credit allowance and regulatory measures. Its scoped prudential reconciliation constructs the allowance-cap base before excess deductions and leaves missing leverage averages unresolved. The richer loss formula retains exposure/severity dependence. Asset classification now distinguishes amortised cost, debt/equity FVOCI and FVTPL; a modified-time-value example begins the contractual cash-flow test and continues next.
exit_state: Classification requires management and contractual evidence before loan methods are selected. Expected loss uses disjoint default events and later cash shortfalls. A commitment draw conditions funding uncertainty while preserving original credit history and moves provision into allowance atomically. The next funded-loan example has reached year-one SICR and a separate credit-impairment event; its recovery and write-off sequence continues next.
findings: Missing documents in this system are not treated as proof that a holder could not perform the contractual assessment required by a standard.
The ECL discussion distinguishes the default-event horizon from later cash losses and refuses equal-weight probabilities for an unweighted history set.
The commitment example derives the funded allowance4 by conditioning the joint probabilities, retains SICR and removes the old provision without double loss.
The funded-loan opening separates survival conditioning from an authored forecast revision and distinguishes default from a missed instalment when no instalment is due. No new confirmed local defect.
